issues.description: Typo 'stlib' instead of 'stdlib' in the deprecation docstring ships to user-facing docs.
issues.detail: The new `.. deprecated:: 4.3` directive reads 'Use the stlib's' instead of 'stdlib's'. It's a one-character fix that should land in this same patch rather than as a follow-up. Trivial to correct before merge.

issues.description: Deprecation message should show how to replace the combined stdout+stderr redirect case.
issues.detail: The retired wrapper let callers redirect both streams in a single with-block; the stdlib replacement requires nesting two context managers or using ExitStack. Without a one-line example in the deprecation message or docstring, users will reach for the familiar shape rather than the decomposed one. Close the migration gap explicitly.

issues.description: Deprecation test only exercises the stdout branch and loosely matches the warning text.
issues.detail: The new test asserts the warning fires and that stdout redirection still works, but never covers the stderr branch the wrapper also redirects. Tightening `match=` to pin the version string and adding a stderr assertion would prevent a careless refactor from silently breaking one branch during the remaining release window.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on ACCEPT with minor polish. This is a small, well-scoped deprecation of `falcon.testing.redirected` in favor of stdlib context managers — a clean simplification that decomposes an incidentally-complected wrapper, with internal call sites migrated and a news fragment included. The only consensus issues are cosmetic and documentation polish: a 'stlib' typo in the docstring, missing migration guidance for the combined stdout+stderr case, and a deprecation test that under-covers the stderr branch and loosely matches the warning. None block merge.
